look_here_first: This one should jump out from ground level: a flat, essentially stemless rosette produces a large yellow four-petaled flower on an extraordinarily long, sharply 4-angled floral tube.
project_tracker_diagnostic: annual taprooted flat rosette; acaulous/essentially stemless and usually under 10 cm tall; only basal irregularly pinnately lobed leaves; large radial yellow flower about 50–55 mm across; very long square 4-angled floral tube up to about 97 mm; 4 stamens in the Williamson County treatment; large 4-winged many-seeded capsule

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County lists Oenothera triloba among plants occurring naturally and not introduced. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes Oenothera triloba. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment of Oenothera triloba.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Oenothera speciosa: Both have large primrose-type flowers, but O. triloba is a flat stemless rosette with yellow flowers and an extremely long square tube; O. speciosa is leafy-stemmed, spreading/rhizomatous, and usually pink/white. Oenothera macrocarpa: Both can have large yellow flowers and long tubes, but O. triloba is a tiny flat rosette with strongly lobed basal leaves; O. macrocarpa forms a larger leafy plant and develops a very large winged capsule.
